owner: existing Powerhouse Security Operations / original Supabase backend data owner
root_cause: 2026-09-03 legacy PW MO14 assessment intake created SELECT/INSERT RLS policies with true predicates for anon and authenticated roles, causing broad public Data API read/write access to player assessment and lineup tables. The table contained 5 actual assessments on audit day.

source_evidence.client_compatibility_review: Existing public pw-mo14-1.netlify.app original homepage JS data.js/player.js/team.js/sync.js did not reference either table; the active zaal/veld coach uses local device state, not these data API paths.
source_evidence.risk_after: Legacy direct-anonymous review submission is no longer permitted. Future shared coaching assessment requires a server-authorized, authenticated, row-scoped API; do not silently regrant anon.

correction.approach: reversible REVOKE ALL from anon and authenticated, DROP permissive select and insert policies, preserve all data and service_role privileges
correction.verification: Supabase direct readback of effective table privileges and policies after migration

prevention: Never expose named minor player assessment/observations through anon SELECT.
Do not use TO anon/authenticated WITH CHECK true for write access to youth player evaluation data.
Require authenticated user plus tenant/team row ownership for any future data API access; service role only on trusted backend.
Check effective database grants and RLS policy expressions, not just relrowsecurity flags.
For emergency fixes, record exact provider migration and synchronize the original GitHub migration-history lock; protected source merge remains independently OPEN.
next_action: Protect source migration through existing branch and PR checks; for shared review capabilities create user-bound Auth/RLS with server-side rate limits and abuse monitoring, not generic anonymous policies.
